newsitem.title: SPAIN: FOCUS - Telefonica flirts with U.S. suitors.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Telefonica flirts with U.S. suitors.

text.p: Spanish telecommunications group Telefonica de Espana played coy on Thursday with a bevy of U.S. suitors, but said it should find a partner within six weeks.

Chairman Juan Villalonga confirmed that his recently privatised company was in talks with major U.S. telecommunications groups. But he said Telefonica could afford to be choosy and set the pace of the talks.
"Telefonica is the pretty little girl who all the top U.S. telecoms groups want to join up with," he said.

"We are keeping all our options open. It's true that I see the chairman of AT&T Corp, but I've also met with the chairmen of GTE Corp, MCI, British Telecommunications and Southwestern Bell Corp," he told reporters.
"It's true that Telefonica needs a partner in the United States. So I think that we will find one in the next four, five or six weeks," he said.
Telefonica is attractive because it has extensive Latin American holdings through its international subsidiary TISA, which had sales in the region last year of 350 billion pesetas ($2.4 billion).
"AT&T is a very important girlfriend for Telefonica but it is not a marriage," said Villalonga.
The group's silence on its future alliances has raised alarm abroad.

Reports of a possible deal for a pan-American network between Telefonica and Concert, a joint venture planned between BT and MCI, upset the Spanish group's current allies who thought it was fraternising with the enemy.
Telefonica is already part of another global alliance -- Unisource, a principally European consortium directed by a prime BT rival, AT&T.

Unisource -- which also includes Sweden's Telia, Swiss Telecom and Koninklijke PTT Nederland of the Netherlands -- said any Telefonica plans to associate with a competitor such as BT-MCI could be grounds for a divorce.
"This could be a complicating factor or so grave that we would not accept it," Paul Smits, the president of Unisource told a Dutch newspaper on Tuesday.
AT&T is also worried. Chief executive John Walter will visit Madrid in the coming days to try to bring Telefonica back into line.
Some analysts preferred a change of alliance. Any link between Telefonica and Concert "would have strategic value for everyone involved", said an SBC Warburg report.

"Concert would become a large global operator while Telefonica will not only join the principal international alliance, but will also raise the strategic value of its investments in Latin America," the report said.
A Madrid-based analyst added that Telefonica had not gained from its participation in Unisource, which lost more than 20 billion pesetas in the first nine months of 1996.
